### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e2e4f568803ba2fe617c227ec45516a2a7cb7af` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `67712db0f7c9a69900906cd980e1eb5edd1c5abe` — the merge of head `df7593e75a68ba34211c5363793b36ccdfbc0706` into base `0e2e4f568803ba2fe617c227ec45516a2a7cb7af`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 67712db0f7c9a69900906cd980e1eb5edd1c5abe && git checkout 67712db0f7c9a69900906cd980e1eb5edd1c5abe
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0e2e4f568803ba2fe617c227ec45516a2a7cb7af df7593e75a68ba34211c5363793b36ccdfbc0706 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0e2e4f568803ba2fe617c227ec45516a2a7cb7af && git merge --no-ff df7593e75a68ba34211c5363793b36ccdfbc0706

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e2e4f568803ba2fe617c227ec45516a2a7cb7af
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ece703ea4c593b1ac293708aa9e9b5faec12f834`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/bulk-action.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/bulk-action.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json, packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json, packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json, packages/spec/json-schema.manifest/ui.json, .changeset/34216-bulk-action-result.md, content/docs/references/ui/bulk-action.mdx, content/docs/references/index.mdx, docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md, docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/ui.md + read, not reviewed: ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useBulkExecutor.ts, ui/packages/types/src/data.ts, ui/packages/types/src/objectql.ts, packages/spec/src/api/batch.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/picklist.zod.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts, AGENTS.md

Read at 2026-11-16T03:22Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6906315985; hand-off 6906299911 and lane request 6906307069 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). First review of this PR, so no prior finding ids exist; M1, S1, S2, N1 and N2 below are all new. Read against card #34216, seat ruling 6905490575 (option A, resolve-only, spec-only) and hand-off 6906299911.

### ① Derived judgments

The three deviations the lane holds, each judged against the repo's own rule:

1. `Metadata-protocol: added` in place of the claim's `none`: **holds**. The authorable-surface generator lists the top-level keys of every exported object schema, wire shapes included: `api/BatchUpdateResponse:*` and `data/HookContext:*` already sit on that surface, so `ui/BulkActionResult:failed` and `:succeeded` land there by the generator's standing behaviour, not by a misclassification of this shape. `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `none` over a moved `authorable-surface/` shard and forbids editing a baseline to quiet it, so `added` is the only kind the gate accepts. It is also the honest kind in substance: the party that writes this value is the author of an action's handler body, which AGENTS.md step 3 covers as "a new key" an author can write. A separate non-authorable export class does not exist in the generator today; inventing one is not this PR's job.
2. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: **holds**. Three new exports from `@objectstack/spec/ui`, nothing removed or refused. The gate's own rule is that `added` cannot sit under `Clause-②: no`, and the arm must be one of the closed pair, so the claim's "additive optional shape" wording had to become `(widening)`.
3. Strictness ledger row `bulk-action.zod.ts` authorable to mixed, strip count unchanged: **holds by the ledger's counting rule**. The row sits in the `ui/` file-level triage table, whose `Class` cell is free prose; the machine-read grammar that demands a stated split (`mixed · n authorable`) binds the remaining-strip map only, and this file has no strip site and no row there. The counts shard moves 221 to 223 sites and passthrough 4 to 6, with strict 212 and strip 5 unchanged, which is exactly two new `looseObject` sites. `mixed` with a served or runtime half left loose is the same verdict the `picklist.zod.ts` and `hook.zod.ts` rows carry.

Generated artifacts against the source, read not run: `api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json` gain the three exports; `declaration-map/ui.json` gains the schema and its input type and omits `BulkActionResultParsed`, as it omits every other `*Parsed` type; `json-schema.manifest/ui.json` gains `ui/BulkActionResult`; `authorable-surface/ui.json` gains the two top-level keys; the references index moves 176 to 177 ui schemas and 1663 to 1664 overall. All consistent with one new exported object schema.

The reference page `content/docs/references/ui/bulk-action.mdx` is true to the schema: both lists required, `failed[number]` with required `id` and `message`, the entry rendered as open. It repeats the describe text, so it inherits M1.

Tests: the accept, refuse and loose-member pins are real and each ablation leg in the PR body maps to one of them. The two "a rejection stays the one-outcome report" cases pass for any object that lacks the two lists, so they pin nothing about rejections; see N2.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor, with `Metadata-protocol: added` and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on both the PR body and the changeset body. AGENTS.md step 3: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. The level is right. No breaking arm, so no ADR-0087 disposition and no migration mapping is owed; the changeset's FROM/TO paragraph is voluntary, and its last sentence is the subject of M1.

CI on this head at read time: 69 check-runs, 27 success, 12 skipped, 30 still in progress, none failed. Finished and green: both `Check Changeset` runs, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Build Docs`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, both PR-body guards. Still running: `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1 to 8, `Test UI` 1 to 16, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`. The spec suite and the generated-artifact check ride the running jobs, so CI is not yet evidence for them. The PR is still a draft. This record is a FAIL on M1 regardless of how those runs end.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Spec-only diff: no file under `ui/`, `packages/runtime` or any other package. Matches the ruling.
- File surface beyond the claim: `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md`, declared in the PR body. Accepted: the row is the hand-written half the regenerated counts shard depends on.
- `Skills-docs` names follow-up #34268, which exists and is open in `domain:skills`. It waits on the ui reader, which has no card (M1).
- No security-touching hunk: the diff declares a data shape and reads no credential, permission or tenant boundary.
- Out of this PR, already noted by the seat: the action invocation audit row records `succeeded` for a 200 that carries failed rows. It also has no card yet.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/bulk-action.zod.ts` against ruling 6905490575 and its first consumer:

The shape is what the ruling ordered: name, file, members, whole resolve value, loose at both levels, the out-of-selection rule stated in TSDoc and describe. `looseObject` is the repo's convention for a shape a runtime party writes and a reader is handed (`PicklistServedFieldSchema`, `HookContextSchema`), and the ruling asks for extra members to be tolerated, so loose at both levels is right. String-only ids match the dispatch: the grid stringifies every row id before the aggregate call and `ui/packages/types/src/objectql.ts` documents `params._selectedIds` as a string array.

M1 (must-fix) — The PR publishes a contract that nothing reads, tells authors to use it now, and leaves the reader without a card. Nothing in the tree parses with `BulkActionResultSchema`. The only consumer of an aggregate resolve, `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useBulkExecutor.ts` (the aggregate `bulkCall`, about lines 314 to 321 at this head), discards the resolve value and returns `ids.length`, and its comment states the opposite contract: "Partial success has no envelope on this path — a server that cannot cover the whole selection must reject." So at this head, and after this PR merges, a handler that follows the published text and resolves with a non-empty `failed` is reported to the user as every selected row succeeded, where today's throw is reported as a failure. The changeset body, which ships as the package's CHANGELOG, says in the present tense "To report per row, catch each row's failure in the handler and resolve with `{ succeeded, failed }` instead of throwing after a partial move", and the describe text, the reference page and the ledger row all speak of "the reader" that "drops" ids and "falls back" as if it existed ("read only by the grid's bulk reader"). The lane already applied this reasoning to the skill ("teaching it now would advertise an answer the console does not yet render") and then did not apply it to the changeset and the reference page. AGENTS.md Prime Directive 10: never advertise a capability the runtime does not deliver; fix it, trim it or file an issue, and keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement. "Filed after merge" is none of the three. Required before this can pass: (a) the ui reader card exists now and the PR body, the changeset and the TSDoc name it; (b) the changeset, the describe and the ledger row say plainly that the console does not read the value yet, and that until that card lands a handler that cannot cover the whole selection must still reject; the "resolve instead of throwing" instruction moves to the reader's own changeset or is conditioned on it. Landing the reader in the same series would discharge both.

S1 (should-fix) — The contract fixes one reader rule (an id outside the selection is dropped) and leaves the neighbouring cases to whoever writes the reader: an id listed twice, an id in both `succeeded` and `failed`, and a selected id in neither list. Each changes the count the dialog shows, and the schema accepts all three. Since the spec is where the reader's rule is stated, state these too, in the TSDoc and describe.

S2 (should-fix) — "A value that does not parse keeps the one-outcome report" means, on a resolve, a report of full success. That makes every near miss silent: `BatchUpdateResponseSchema`, which the TSDoc cites as the precedent, uses the same two member names as counts (`succeeded: number`, `failed: number`, rows under `results`), and `BulkWriteResult` in `ui/packages/types/src/data.ts` uses `succeeded: number` and `errors[].error`. A handler that returns the answer of the `/data` batch call it just made, or writes `error` for `message`, or returns numeric record ids, fails the parse and has its failed rows reported as succeeded. The names are the seat's ruling and stand; the TSDoc should say that the shape is not `BatchUpdateResponse` and how it differs, and the seat should decide, in this contract, whether a value that carries a `succeeded` or `failed` member and does not parse may be reported as success.

N1 (nit) — The ledger row now opens with "Everything below is the file's authoring half" and keeps the older sentence that `BulkActionParamSchema` and its option entry are "both now `.passthrough()`"; the source at this head has `BulkActionParamSchema` as `strictObject`. The stale sentence predates this PR, but the new lead-in vouches for it.

N2 (nit) — The two rejection cases in `bulk-action.test.ts` assert that an envelope without top-level lists does not parse, which is true of any such object; they document the ruling and pin no behaviour. Fine as documentation; do not count them as coverage of the rejection path.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Prior findings, by id:

- **M1: closed.** Card #34269 exists, is open in `domain:ui`, was filed by the seat, and carries the reader: the parse on an aggregate dispatch, every counting rule the contract states, the rejection left unchanged, pins with a CONTROL, and the duty to remove the planned marker in the same PR. ### ① Derived judgments

No other generated file needed to move, because the delta changed describes and comments only and the manifest, surface and declaration shards do not carry describe text.

Can #34269 implement the rules without guessing? Yes for the count. The three-way read (neither member: today's report; either member and no parse: unreadable; parse: per row) is decidable from the value alone, and the four id rules give one bucket to every selected id: failed if listed in `failed`, else succeeded if listed in `succeeded`, else not confirmed, with out-of-selection ids discarded first and repeats collapsed. Two display points are left open and are listed as N3.

The PR is still a draft and reports a clean merge state.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Spec-only: no file under `ui/`, `packages/runtime` or any other package. Matches the ruling.
- File surface beyond the claim is still only `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md`, declared.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/bulk-action.zod.ts` against ruling 6905490575, the hand-off's S1 and S2 rulings, and its first consumer (#34269):

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The published text now claims exactly what the runtime delivers: a declared shape, no reader, and an instruction that keeps today's correct behaviour (reject). The reader's rules are stated once, in the contract, and the reader card repeats them without drift. Three nits, none of which blocks:

N1 (nit) — The S2 ruling replaces a sentence of ruling 6905490575 ("a value that does not parse falls back to today's one-outcome report"), and that ruling is still the last word on card #34216; the replacement is recorded only in the PR hand-off and in #34269. Follow-up card #34268 still carries the old sentence ("a return value that is not this shape falls back to today's report"), so the skills lane would teach the superseded rule. The seat should amend the ruling on the card and correct #34268. The PR body's `Skills-docs` line also no longer names #34268, which the previous head's hand-off said it did. New at this head.

N2 (nit) — The PR body still says the shape is "not a reserved key". After the S2 ruling the two names are meaningful at the top level of any aggregate resolve: once the reader lands, a handler whose own summary uses `succeeded` or `failed` in another form moves from the success report to the unreadable report.
